# Judges Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_287.jpg

1. And there was a man from the hill-country of Ephrayim, and his name [was] Mikhayehu.

2. And he said to his mother, "The eleven hundred [pieces] of silver that were taken from you, and [about which] you spoke a curse — and also spoke [it] in my ears — behold, the silver [is] with me; I took it." And his mother said, "Blessed [be] my son by YHWH."

3. And he returned the eleven hundred [pieces] of silver to his mother. And his mother said, "I surely consecrate the silver to YHWH from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image. And now, I return it to you."

4. And he returned the silver to his mother, and his mother took two hundred [pieces] of silver and gave them to the silversmith. And he made it into a carved image and a cast image, and it was in the house of Mikhayehu.

5. And the man Mikhah had a house of God. And he made an ephod and teraphim, and he filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became his priest.

6. In those days there was no king in Yisrael. Each man did the right in his own eyes.

7. And there was a young man from Beit-Lechem of Y'hudah, from the clan of Y'hudah, and he [was] a Levite, and he was sojourning there.

8. And the man went from the city, from Beit-Lechem of Y'hudah, to sojourn wherever he could find [a place]. And he came to the hill-country of Ephrayim, to the house of Mikhah, making his way.

9. And Mikhah said to him, "From where do you come?" And he said to him, "I [am] a Levite from Beit-Lechem of Y'hudah, and I am going to sojourn wherever I can find [a place]."

10. And Mikhah said to him, "Dwell with me and be to me a father and a priest, and I will give you ten [pieces] of silver per year and a set of garments and your food." And the Levite went.

11. And the Levite was content to dwell with the man, and the young man was to him like one of his sons.

12. And Mikhah filled the hand of the Levite, and the young man became his priest, and he was in the house of Mikhah.

13. And Mikhah said, "Now I know that YHWH will do good to me, because the Levite has become my priest."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **v.2 — "eleven hundred pieces of silver":** The same amount offered by each Philistine lord to Delilah (16:5). The verbal echo connects the two stories: stolen silver, religious corruption, tribal collapse.

2. **v.5 — "he filled the hand":** vaymalle et-yad — a technical term for priestly ordination ("to fill the hand" = to consecrate/install as priest). Micah ordains his own son — a non-Levite — as priest of his private shrine.

3. **v.6 — "each man did the right in his own eyes":** ish hayyashar b'einav ya'aseh — the refrain that frames chapters 17-21. The same phrase yashar b'einav was used of Samson (14:3). The entire book has been building to this verdict.

— EMET, AI Translator
